newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHERS TOP TIMES AS RAIN HITS PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHERS TOP TIMES AS RAIN HITS PRACTICE.

text.p: Ralf Schumacher of Germany upstaged his older brother and double world champion Michael in Friday's opening practice for Sunday's German Grand Prix but the times meant little as the weather dominated proceedings.
The first session had started with a damp track that quickly dried but the drivers managed only a few quick laps before the rain returned near the end of the hour-long session.
Just before the start of the second session, however, the rain came down much more heavily and flooded parts of the track, meaning the drivers did not venture out for the first 10 minutes.

The conditions eventually improved to leave the track almost dry near the end of the session but the best times were still more than one second slower than Ralf Schumacher's fastest lap of one minute 46.196 seconds from the first session.
The Jordan driver ended his second session in the barriers after a spin at the Ayrton Senna curve.
Michael Schumacher, driving a Ferrari, was second quickest in 1:46.322. The two brothers would one day probably end up on the same team, Ralf was quoted as saying on Friday.
"I don't know what I'll be doing in two, five, 10 years. But one thing I'm convinced of: one day Michael and I will become team mates," Ralf told Belgium's Het Nieuwsblad newspaper.
Briton Johnny Herbert was third fastest on 1:46.517 with the best top speed of 342 kph.
World champion Damon Hill, of Britain, was eighth fastest overall on 1:47.542 in his TWR Arrows. He had a spin in the stadium complex during the wet second session but was able to continue.

Finn Mika Hakkinen, driving for McLaren, was the only driver in the top 10 to improve his time in the second session, after an engine problem meant he failed to complete a quick lap during first practice. REUTER
